description: Single source of truth for threat-modeling-prefill. Holds (a) the pre-fill rules that map architecture signals (from the DAT + dataflow) to candidate STRIDE-LM scenarios, (b) the STRIDE-LM category reference, (c) the risk scales, and (d) the STRIDE-LM -> NIST SP 800-53 family mapping. Read by assets/scripts/build-threatmodel.ps1 AND cited by any generated doc/README. Never duplicate this table into a .md or hard-code it in a script. All generated scenarios are CANDIDATES to validate with the security team - never acquired.

engine.note: The module embeds no intelligence of its own: scenario wording is produced by an explicit model call (Bedrock by default; SFS Assist only as an optional conversational layer if a dialog need is confirmed). The deterministic part (signal detection, risk scale, NIST mapping) lives here.

countermeasureEffectiveness.label: Strong - defense in depth, enforced and monitored

prefillRules.signal: An API / edge endpoint is exposed (API gateway, public or partner-facing endpoint, REST/HTTP exposure).
candidateScenarios: Spoofing of a client / token at the API edge (stolen or forged credential).
Tampering of a request in transit or broken access control at the edge (parameter/authorization bypass).
typicalCountermeasures: mTLS / strong auth at the edge

prefillRules.signal: File-based or batch exchanges (SFTP, object drops, scheduled jobs, backup copy/restore between accounts).
candidateScenarios: Repudiation of a file transfer / batch action (no tamper-evident log of who moved what, when).
Denial of Service via oversized / malformed / flooding batch input or dependency unavailability.

prefillRules.signal: Personal / sensitive data (PII) is identified in the flows or stored data (DCP = Yes, or evidence/logs that can contain PII).
candidateScenarios: Information Disclosure of personal data (unauthorized read, over-broad access, data left unencrypted or exported insecurely).
prefillRules.linkedRequirement: Data Privacy requirement (GDPR) - cross-check with dict-assessment DICT=C and the DPO.

prefillRules.signal: Tight coupling to the shared infrastructure / Landing Zone (cross-account roles, shared services, trust relationships, SCP-governed access).
candidateScenarios: Elevation of Privilege through an over-permissive cross-account role or trust path.
Lateral Movement from a compromised component into the Landing Zone or into other accounts.
prefillRules.note: DEDICATED ALERT: infra/Landing-Zone coupling is a recurrent ARB refusal motive - always surface this scenario explicitly and flag it high for the security review.
